transport: JSON-RPC 2.0 over the Unix socket or WebSocket (?token=...). Standard ACP methods pass through to the session's agent; _acpmux/* methods are the multiplexer's own.

acpNotes.initialize: The result's _meta.acpmux carries auth (the proof this connection presented, server/conn_auth.rs: localSocket|listenerToken|localApp|peerToken; a connection with none gets error -32001 for its first request and is closed), personInstance (this daemon run's id, which decision proofs bind; cx-0q7o), operations: string[] (the handoff and permission-group methods this daemon serves; clients gate each UI on its methods) and handoff: {maxCapsuleBytes: 65536}. features includes permissionGroups when permission groups are available.
acpNotes.session/new: params._meta.acpmux.adopt {harness?: string, agentSessionId: string, ifLive?: "refuse" | "fork" | "open"} adopts a Claude Code or Codex session started outside acpmux: the id must be a bare id found in the harness's own store (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or ~/.claude projects, CODEX_HOME or ~/.codex sessions), else invalid params. cwd defaults to the session's recorded cwd (Claude refuses a different one). The first turn resumes it (claude --resume, or session/load). Adopting an id twice returns the existing acpmux session. A session live in another process (a process outside acpmux whose command line names the id, or a transcript written in the last 2 minutes) is refused with error data {reason: "adopt.live", details: {signal: "process" | "recentWrite", pid?, command?, agoSeconds?, canFork}} unless ifLive is "open" (adopt anyway) or "fork" (Claude only: a new conversation from claude --resume <id> --fork-session). Recorded as mux adopted {agentSessionId, fork?: true}. A harness name that is a folder profile (.cmux/harnesses/<id>.toml in cwd or a parent; BRING-YOUR-OWN-HARNESS H4) that may not start yet is refused with invalid params; data {reason: harness.needs_trust (answer the folder's Trust question) | harness.needs_enable (show the Enable harness sheet: _acpmux/harness_enable), harness: string (the id), folder: string (the canonical folder that holds .cmux/harnesses)}. A Web or peer connection and an invalid file get no data.
acpNotes.session/prompt: params._meta.acpmux {promptId?: string, steer?: boolean, provenance?: {kind: "agent_message", from: string, fromName?: string, to: string, msgId: string, threadId: string, replyTo?: string}}. provenance names the agent that sent the prompt (cmux agent message): each field one line, ids and addresses 1 to 256 bytes, fromName 1 to 64 characters, unknown fields dropped; it is recorded as _meta.provenance on the user_message (and queued) record, never sent to the agent. Only the unix socket may send it: any other origin gets data.reason provenance.origin_refused, a malformed one provenance.value_refused; a prompt forwarded to a peer goes without it. On Claude Code harnesses a text block's cache_control reaches the API unchanged; other extra block fields are dropped. The response stays at the end of the turn and gains _meta.acpmux {promptId, turnId, turnSeq} next to the agent's own _meta. The prompting connection gets _acpmux/prompt_accepted as soon as the prompt is recorded.
acpNotes.session/cancel: A notification, as ACP defines it. Sent as a request (with an id) it is answered with {} once the cancel reaches the agent, also when no turn runs.
acpNotes.session/update: Live agent updates arrive with sessionId set to the acpmux id and _meta.acpmux {seq, at, kind} merged into the agent's own _meta (the agent's keys are kept). session/load replays add replay: true.

_acpmux/btw.errors: invalid params: an empty question, a model that is not a string, an explicit model the harness refuses; data.reason btw.remote: a Web connection or a peer; data.reason btw.no_read_only_mode ("this agent has no read-only mode"): the codex-acp adapter, opencode, or a family with no asking mode, before anything opens; data.reason btw.mode_unset: the mode could not be set and confirmed, the side session discarded; not found: an unknown chat
_acpmux/btw.note: The composer's /btw (hub/btw.rs): a side session in the chat's harness and folder, tagged side with the chat (the lists hide it), titled with the question (first line, 80 chars). Read-only: policy approve-reads (ask or deny-all when the chat's is that) with rules that refuse every tool kind but read, search, fetch and think; The session runs in a mode set and confirmed in its reported current mode: readOnly mode for one that reads only (Claude plan, Codex in process read-only: sandbox read-only, approvals on-request), readOnly policy for another family's first asking mode (webAskingModes), which asks before every change for the rules to refuse. A profile that runs opencode or codex-acp under family claude is refused, and while one is configured Claude's own /btw is refused too (fail closed). The confirm reads acpmux's own record after a successful session/set_mode, not a readback from the agent; a pane or the socket can still re-mode a side session (the person's choice); respawn replays the mode for ACP harnesses without failing on a refusal. Harness-side: Claude permissions.allow still applies in plan mode, and Codex MCP tools run outside its sandbox. The transcript context is marked untrusted, not instructions, and every closing tag inside it (any case, whitespace around the slash or before >) is made inert. Claude and Codex fork through the chat's latest finished turn, also while a turn runs; any other harness, or a chat with no finished turn, starts a new session whose first prompt carries the chat's newest transcript (at most 12 KiB) as hidden context (prompt_context.rs). The question is sent as its first prompt; the reply comes once the prompt is recorded, before the answer. The chat is never paused, cancelled or changed.

_acpmux/stats.note: Local unix socket only (hq#1920): counts and times, never prompt or tool text. One offset applies to the whole range, so days before a DST change shift by an hour. A turn or wait the daemon lost when it died ends at the session's last record before the loss: at the restart's own record (turn_result detail outcome_unknown, or status idle detail restart, which a restart writes for a session it found waiting), or at the end of the log when this daemon does not hold the session running or waiting; older logs without the restart record end such a wait at the next status. A prompt ends a wait left after its turn at the prompt's time. A prompt that never got turn_started and never settled counts as a prompt, not a turn. A steer sent again as the next prompt (same promptId) counts once, as the prompt. A fork's log starts with copies of its parent's prompts, tool calls and turns before its forked record: they count only in the parent's log, in every total, day, hour, streak and peakParallel, and not at all once that log is gone.

_acpmux/prewarm.note: Hints the harness the pane is about to switch to. After the debounce (pool.debounceMs, default 150) only the newest hint counts: a hidden session for it starts in that cwd (agent host, initialize and the harness session done). Per cwd at most two are kept: the harness used before the current one and the hinted one. A session/new of exactly that shape (cwd, harness, preset, argv, system prompt, env and credentials, account) takes it at once. Hidden sessions never appear in _acpmux/sessions or liveAgents and leave nothing in the store unless taken; _acpmux/status pool lists them as {entries: [{harness, preset, cwd, roles, state}], rssBytes}. They exit after pool.idleMinutes (default 10) unused, under pool.maxRssMb (default 1024, oldest first) and at shutdown.

params.signal: term|kill? (Claude Code stops a task one way: both send its stop_task)

_acpmux/process/kill.errors: invalid params: a malformed processId or signal, or a chat that is not Claude Code's; not found: no such process
_acpmux/process/kill.note: Asks the harness to stop the process; the end arrives as a process_update (killed, reason person). A process that already ended is left alone, and one whose harness is gone is marked lost; a kill never starts a harness. Unix socket and local app only.

result.msgId: string (the provenance msgId, else the promptId)
result.already: true? (a repeat: the first withdraw's outcome again)

_acpmux/prompt_withdraw.errors: data.reason withdraw.not_found (-32002): the session's log holds no such prompt; withdraw.not_a_message (-32602): the prompt has no provenance (the person's own); withdraw.edited (-32602): the person edited the queued message (_acpmux/queue_edit update), which made it theirs; withdraw.notice_failed (-32000): the retraction notice was refused or not recorded within 5 s, nothing recorded, withdraw again; withdraw.origin_refused (invalid params): any connection but the unix socket (Web, LocalApp, Peer, via web); transfer.moving while the chat is moved; never forwarded to a peer
_acpmux/prompt_withdraw.note: cmux agent message's unsend (hub/withdraw.rs, cx-55d27). unsent: the prompt still waited (queued or held); it leaves the queue with queue_removed {reason: withdrawn}, its session/prompt answers cancelled with _meta.acpmux.withdrawn, and it never runs, a restart included (the queue is rebuilt from the log). retracted: its turn runs; prompt_retracted is recorded and a notice ("The message <msgId> from <from> was withdrawn by its sender; disregard it.", promptId <promptId>.withdrawn.<uuid>, the sender's provenance with msgId <msgId>.withdrawn and replyTo <msgId>) is steered into the turn when the agent steers, else queued at the head of the queue. prompt_retracted is written only once the notice is recorded. too_late: its turn ended (turn_result, or prompt_refused); nothing changes. The prompt is followed by its promptId into the turn that ran it (a send_now steer, or a steer run as the next turn). A repeat changes nothing either and answers already: true (unsent stays unsent; a retracted message gets no second notice).

params._meta.acpmux.answeredBy: {device, feedItem}? (each 1 to 128 of [A-Za-z0-9_.:-]; the person's own connection only: the app answering for a device the person answered on; recorded as permission_decision answeredBy, never sent to the agent; from any other connection permission.person_required, malformed invalid params)
params._meta.acpmux.personDecision: string? (64 lowercase hex: HMAC-SHA256(key, "acpmux-person-decision-v1" 0 personInstance 0 sessionId 0 permissionId 0 optionId 0 decisionNonce); lets an allow relayed from another machine's app count on a connection that is not the person, once per nonce, never with answers; cx-0q7o. For a peer's session the daemon that mirrors it forwards every answer (allow, deny, cancel) and the peer decides with its own key and rules; the forward adds _meta.acpmux.peerHops (at most 4 forwards, then invalid params). With a proof that counts, answeredBy is accepted from a connection that is not the person)

_acpmux/permission_respond.errors: -32000 with data.reason permission.person_required: an allow (any option that is not a reject_*) from a connection that did not present this launch's person key and carries no valid decision proof for the pending prompt (hub/person.rs); the prompt stays pending. Deny and cancel are open to every client.

params.key: string (64 lowercase hex: the app's per-launch person key)

_acpmux/person_enroll.errors: data.reason person.enroll_refused: not the unix socket, or the peer's audit token is not the signed app that contains this daemon; person.enroll_unavailable: an unsigned daemon whose spawn key (--person-key-fd) is another key (start a new daemon with this key)
_acpmux/person_enroll.note: Only the person may allow or widen what runs without asking (hub/person.rs). The key never crosses a socket after enrollment (cx-fcaq): a unix socket or LocalApp connection whose FIRST request is initialize gets _meta.acpmux.personChallenge {nonce, connection}, and becomes the person when its SECOND request is _acpmux/person_prove with the HMAC of that challenge and its own transport under the current key (a personKey field is stripped and never read). Without it: permission_respond allow, permission_group_respond allow_once|allow_chat, set_policy / set_default_policy / defaults / presets with a policy other than ask or deny-all or a spawn env, set_rules that could auto-approve, session/set_mode or set_config_option to a mode the asking table does not list, any set_rules on a session whose policy does not ask, a defaults or presets write that removes a stored policy (clear, or policy null), an _acpmux/tag write of the handoffKey tag, and a session method acpmux does not handle (the harness catch-all) are refused with data.reason permission.person_required. handoff_prepare never adopts a tagged target wider than its policy (key_conflict). initialize's _meta.acpmux.person reports it.

params.nonce: string (64 lowercase hex: the app's fresh 32-byte nonce)

result.proof: string (64 lowercase hex: HMAC-SHA256(key, "acpmux-person-holds-v1" 0 instance 0 nonce))

_acpmux/person_holds.errors: invalid params: not the unix socket, or a malformed nonce; -32000 data.reason person.no_key: this run holds no person key; person.holds_limit: more than 8 calls on this connection
_acpmux/person_holds.note: hub/person.rs, cx-0q7o slice 2c: the app checks, over a nonce of its own, that a daemon it started holds ITS key before it relays an allow there. Its own domain: the answer is never a decision or connection proof. The 8-per-connection limit is not a security bound. Threat model: remote approvals stop agents and scripts that cannot write the remote user's home folder or cmux-tui binary; an agent that runs as the same user and can write those files can capture the key on the next restart.

params.proof: string (64 lowercase hex: HMAC-SHA256(key, "acpmux-person-v1" 0 transport 0 nonce 0 connection), transport unix or app as the client knows it, for this connection's personChallenge)

_acpmux/person_prove.errors: -32000 with data.reason person.proof_refused: not the second request after initialize, no challenge (Web, Peer), or a proof for another challenge or key; the connection stays not the person
_acpmux/person_prove.note: hub/person.rs. Bound to the nonce and the connection id: a proof captured by whatever listens on the socket path proves nothing on another connection.

_acpmux/permission_groups.note: Read on reconnect/lag before retrying an identical decision body/key. Unknown groupId is not_found.

_acpmux/permission_group_respond.errors: collecting, stale_revision, already_resolved, policy_changed (-32000, data.group); key_conflict (-32602); not_found (-32002)
_acpmux/permission_group_respond.note: Atomically validates sealed membership and single-use options before responding to any underlying ACP request. allow_chat grants later eligible requests in this chat until agent stop/restart; deny policy/rules override and grants never copy to fork/handoff. Repeat identical key/body replays a retained receipt; another body conflicts. Interactive and unknown requests remain individual.

_acpmux/permission_chat_revoke.note: Revokes future chat approvals; already accepted operations are not undone.

params.rules: {autoApprove?: string[], autoDeny?: string[], ask?: string[], default?: 'approve'|'deny'|'ask'} | null

result.applied: now|afterTurn|nextStart (now: the idle chat's Claude Code restarted on it and resumed; afterTurn: a turn runs, and its process restarts when it ends; nextStart: no process runs, and the next start takes it)

_acpmux/set_tools.errors: data.reason tools.immutable: the harness takes its tools when the chat starts (toolsMutable false: every ACP harness; refused without starting the chat); tools.fixed: canToggle false (a skill, a plugin, or a server the user's own Claude config turned off); tools.remote: a remote WebSocket connection (only the app or the unix socket); code -32002: no such row
_acpmux/set_tools.note: Records the chat's choice for one MCP server: every start of its Claude Code gets --disallowedTools mcp__<server> for each server that is off, so it survives respawn, resume and daemon restart, and a fork keeps it. Claude Code's mcp_toggle is never sent (it persists into ~/.claude.json for every session in the folder). Watchers get _acpmux/session_changed kind tools. initialize lists the feature toolInventory (cx-thur3).

_acpmux/archive.note: The chat menu's Archive (true: sets the `archived` tag to now in milliseconds; the lists hide the chat) or Unarchive (false: removes it). One tag with one value, so a page relay allows it without reading tag names (cx-jlzsf).

_acpmux/side.note: New side chat: tags the fork sessionId `side` with the chat's session id (the lists hide it). Refused for a chat that is the fork itself or unknown (cx-jlzsf).

params.harness: string (the target: a family or profile of another harness)
params.handoffKey: string (repeat safety: the same key returns the same record and never a second target)

_acpmux/handoff_prepare.errors: source_busy (a turn runs, prompts are queued or a permission waits), same_harness, policy_unmappable, checkpoint_unattested, key_conflict (-32602, with handoff: the handoffKey already names a handoff from another source or to another harness)
_acpmux/handoff_prepare.note: Captures the source's transcript up to its current seq, newest messages first within maxCapsuleBytes (the oldest are cut), and creates the target session in the source's cwd with the source's policy (same) or the next stricter one (narrower: approve-all > approve-edits > approve-reads > ask > deny-all). Same or narrower is guaranteed for the acpmux permission policy only, not for harness modes, which are not mapped across harnesses. The target is tagged handoffKey=<key>; a repeat prepare whose record was never saved adopts that live, never-prompted target instead of creating a second one. Sends no prompt to the target and never modifies the source.

_acpmux/handoff_get.note: With sessionId: the handoff the session is the target of, else the newest one not discarded that it is the source of, else null (an ordinary session). After a reconnect, read this before retrying anything.

params.checkpoint: CheckpointInput | null ? (absent keeps it, null clears it)

_acpmux/handoff_draft.errors: stale_revision (with handoff), not_draft (with handoff), discarded (with handoff), checkpoint_unattested, capsule_too_large, not_found
_acpmux/handoff_draft.note: The same draftKey again (one of the last 8 writes) answers with the revision and capsule that write produced, state and updatedAt current, and never writes twice. A stale revision whose content equals the current draft succeeds without a new revision; other content is refused with stale_revision.

params.capsule: {text: string, memoryRefs?: string[]}? (absent keeps the draft)

_acpmux/handoff_start.errors: checkpoint_required, checkpoint_unattested, stale_revision (with handoff), capsule_too_large, already_started (another promptId after the first start; with handoff), discarded (with handoff), not_found
_acpmux/handoff_start.note: Records state starting with the promptId, then sends the capsule text (plus a block naming the checkpoint and memory references) to the target once, as session/prompt with _meta.acpmux {promptId, resend: true}, and answers once the target records the prompt (the turn runs on). After a timeout, read handoff_get; in state starting or started, call start again with the same promptId: the daemon finds the prompt in the record or the target's log (also after a restart) and answers already_started without sending again. A start refused before the target records the prompt returns the record to draft and keeps its promptId, which a later start reuses by default. Test-only fault (uncertain_delivery is produced only by this hook): with ACPMUX_TEST_DROP_HANDOFF_START_REPLY=1 in the daemon's environment a first start sends the prompt, leaves the record starting and answers an error with reason uncertain_delivery instead of the receipt, so a retry exercises reconciliation.

_acpmux/handoff_discard.note: Closes the target, which has never been prompted. The source stays intact. Discarding twice is fine.

_acpmux/event.note: Every mux record of an attached session. With attach eventStream: every record that passes kinds, agent session/update notifications included (the original notification in msg, its sessionId the agent's own).

params.kind: string (the record kind, or queue for queued/dequeued, permission_resolved for permission_auto, purged)

_acpmux/session_changed.note: For watchers: status, queue, permission, turn and policy changes, and peer sessions that appear, change or leave.

_acpmux/harnesses_changed.note: To watchers (_acpmux/watch) when a harness profile file, a managed or user profile folder, or cmux.json changed and the catalog reloaded (debounced 200 ms, no polling). Ask _acpmux/harnesses for the details. Folder profiles (.cmux/harnesses in a workspace) are not watched and never trigger it; ask _acpmux/harnesses {cwd} again.

params.decisionNonce: string (new random nonce for this prompt)

_acpmux/permission_pending.note: decisionNonce and personInstance are what a relayed allow's personDecision covers (permission_respond); the answer that counts spends the nonce, a refused answer spends nothing. Also sent for a permission_reissued record: a prompt the next daemon adopted, with a new decisionNonce under the new personInstance (the same permissionId). _acpmux/info pending entries carry both too. To attached connections, and to watchers that are not attached (via: watch). Remote sessions reach watchers only through session_changed.

catalog.changed.note: Sent to every connection (no watch or attach needed) when the model catalog in use changes. Read _acpmux/models or _acpmux/harnesses again.

params.promptId: string (the client's _meta.acpmux.promptId, or one acpmux generated)

_acpmux/prompt_accepted.note: Sent only to the connection that sent session/prompt, as soon as the daemon records the prompt (the queued or user_message record). Not relayed for sessions on a peer.

_acpmux/process_update.note: When a background process starts or ends (its mux process_update record), to connections attached to its session or watching (_acpmux/watch). Never to a remote WebSocket connection or a peer.

CatalogSummary.generatedAt: string (ISO-8601: when the server built it)

PermissionGroup.note: Fixed 100ms window, max32 items; missing single-use allow option makes the group deny-only. Last64 terminal groups retained, pending groups never pruned. See docs/grouped-permissions.md.

SessionDefaults.prefer: string[]? (profiles to use for a family, in order; first installed wins)

HarnessProfile.argv: string[] (${model} = the requested model at spawn)
HarnessProfile.models: (string | {id, name})[] declared catalog, shown ahead of the reported one
HarnessProfile.fallback: string? (profile to move to on limit or auth errors)

SessionSummary.name: string
SessionSummary.stateSeq: number (bumps on status, permission and turn changes)
SessionSummary.unread: boolean (a turn ended while no attached client showed the chat; cleared when one shows it)
SessionSummary.shown: boolean (some attached client shows the chat: _acpmux/attach visible, _acpmux/view)
SessionSummary.indicator: input|working|failed|lost|done|null (the status dot every client draws; first match wins: input = a permission or question waits, working = a turn runs, failed = the last turn failed, lost = the agent process is gone (disconnected or unreachable) and the last turn did not answer, done = the last turn answered (seen is client-side), null = nothing to show)
SessionSummary.lastTurn: {turnId, promptId, status, stopReason?, errorText?, errorSource?, detail?, endedAt} | null
SessionSummary.lane: {state: working|input|idle|failed|lost, since: number|null, error: string|null, step: string|null} | null (a coordinator's view of the session; null when closed: working since its turn started, input since it began waiting, idle since its last turn ended, failed with that turn's errorText, lost when the agent process or peer is gone; step is the running turn's prompt, else the agent's last reply line, one line of at most 240 characters; error and step have secrets masked, e.g. [github token])
SessionSummary.inputSince: number|null (when the session began waiting on the person)
SessionSummary.tools: ToolRow[] (the chat's tools: cmux's own, then what the harness reported)
SessionSummary.toolsMutable: boolean (_acpmux/set_tools can turn its MCP servers off: Claude Code only)
SessionSummary.queue: [{promptId, turnId, client, prompt, queuedAt}] prompts waiting for the running turn

TurnUsage.note: Only what the harness reported: Claude Code reports all of them (its tokens cover the main loop, its cost includes subagents); other harnesses report none, so the fields are absent, never 0. A turn's costUsd is the rise in Claude Code's running total, and is absent when that cannot be told: a failed turn, a total that went down, the first turn of a fork through an earlier turn or of a session older than this field.

ToolRow.canToggle: boolean (an MCP server of a Claude Code chat that its own config did not turn off)

turn_result.detail: string? (outcome_unknown when the daemon restarted mid-turn)
turn_result.model: string? (the session's model when an answered turn ended)

types.EventKinds: string[]: each entry is a category or an exact record kind; a record passes when any entry matches. Categories: transcript (agent session/update except .replay, usage_update, available_commands_update, current_mode_update, config_option_update; plus mux user_message, queued, dequeued, turn_started, turn_result, permission_request, permission_auto, permission_decision, permission_group, permission_chat_allowance, message_superseded, failover, forked, imported, mode, model, stopped, exited), mux (every mux record), wire (in/out requests, responses, harness lines and .replay records), all.

turn_started.note: turnSeq of the turn is this record's seq

turn_end.note: legacy pair of turn_result; turn_error likewise carries {error, code, turnId, turnSeq}

Enforcement.policy: string (always the acpmux permission policy id: ask|approve-reads|approve-edits|approve-all|deny-all, the session's own or the daemon default; comparable across harnesses)
Enforcement.label: native_policy
Enforcement.detail: string|null (names the harness's current mode, e.g. "codex mode read-only; acpmux policy approve-reads; host isolation unverified")

Handoff.target: {sessionId, harness, cwd (the source's), coverage: Coverage[], enforcement: Enforcement}
Handoff.capsule: {text: string (the target's first message, at most maxBytes UTF-8 bytes), context: {fromSeq, toSeq, truncated, bytes (transcript bytes in text), totalBytes (transcript bytes up to toSeq)}, checkpoint: Checkpoint|null, memoryRefs: string[], maxBytes: 65536}
Handoff.turnId: string|null (set once the target records the turn)

HandoffError.data: {reason: source_busy|same_harness|policy_unmappable|checkpoint_required|checkpoint_unattested|capsule_too_large|stale_revision|not_draft|already_started|discarded|not_found|key_conflict|uncertain_delivery (test hook only), handoff?: Handoff}; capsule_too_large adds {limit, bytes}

daemon.readiness: acpmux daemon run binds the socket and --listen address before importing the login shell environment or checking launchers. --ready-fd N writes one line {ready: true, pid, socket, listen, webUrl} to descriptor N and closes it; the log also gets "acpmux ready {...}". _acpmux/status answers at once and reports ready and loginEnv.
daemon.shutdown: The daemon clears any signal mask it inherits, so a launcher that blocks SIGTERM cannot keep it alive. SIGTERM, SIGINT and _acpmux/shutdown remove the socket, detach every agent that runs under an agent host (it keeps running, with its turn and permission prompts, for the next daemon to adopt), stop every other agent (SIGTERM to its process group, SIGKILL to the group after 2 s), save sessions, sync the store and exit, within 5 s. _acpmux/shutdown {endAgents: true} ends hosted agents too, except those of keepSessions, and records each turn in progress as turn_result {status: cancelled, detail: quit}. The CLI follows the same default (cx-qryd0): `acpmux daemon shutdown` keeps hosted agents for the next daemon; `--end-agents` sends endAgents: true; `--keep-agents` is accepted and changes nothing.
